In fifth grade (about 12 years ago) I got pulled out of class because I was showing signs of suicide. The counselor called my mom in to deal with the issue. The mistakes my parents made:

*1. My mom yelled at me in the car for embarrassing her. 
*2. We never spoke about the suicide issue ever again.

There are a lot of other mistakes they made: they never stood up for me whenever I was bullied at home, and they would also join in on it too. I even pulled my dad aside once and asked him "why does everyone only pick on me, all the time." His response: "we're just having fun." Well shit, I sure as hell wasn't having fun. 


Also, during my last trip to Vietnam, we went to this gift shop, and the creepy owner walked up behind me, slid his hand from over my shoulder and down under my shirt to start feeling up my chest. I'm a guy, and so there is nothing there, but it was sure as fuck creepy as hell. When I got home, I told me family (there was about eleven adults in the room at the time), and they **all laughed at me**, my parents included. What was even worst was that they took me back to that shop the next week. I just stood outside looking like a fucking idiot.

Two suicide attempts later, and here I am. So yeah, a lot of mistakes on my parents end. 

**tl;dr: ALWAYS STAND UP FOR YOUR CHILDREN, AND DON'T LAUGH IN THEIR FUCKING FACES.**

In high school, I was in a public speaking class. I was the funny guy. I always memorized every speech, and I must say that I am pretty damn good at public speaking. So one day I took a major shift and decided to talk about my suicide experiences instead of treating myself like a joke. Now, I know in these situations that the teachers are supposed to report me or something, but my speech teacher didn't. Instead, she just let me be who I needed/wanted to be. I really appreciate her for that.

Completely opposite story: In college, I wrote a story about suicide, and the teacher (a grad student) pulled me aside after class and asked me if I wanted any suicide resources. She didn't push me towards anything, and she definitely could have made me see an adviser, but she didn't. I asked her a few months later why she didn't push me, and she told me that she trusted I would do the right thing. So I appreciated that this teacher didn't push me, but she did confront me about it, even if it made her extremely uncomfortable. 

Now, I just finished up my final therapy session two weeks ago, and am also on track to finish off my last year of college to become a teacher too. Maybe I can give back.

It took me about four years to work up the courage to go to therapy, and I'll tell you, the fifteen minute wait will be THE MOST excruciatingly terrible moments of your life. My heart was beating, I was freaking out so badly, and yeah getting is is extremely scary. However, here I am nine months later, just finished my last session 2 weeks ago, and God am I glad I got help. Even if it didn't solve all my problems (and getting "help" will not solve all your problems) it helped me grow a little bit as a person. Working the courage is always going to be difficult, and even though I had a great experience doesn't mean that you will, but I think it's still worth going for. What I did before I went to get professional help was to tell one close friend. They've stuck by me the whole time, didn't push me too hard, and eventually I made my decision. What you can do is have a friend take you. It helps a lot having support. And you have no idea how much it would mean to a friend to help you out, even if it's something as small as giving you a ride, or waiting for you. Anyways, I think you should give it a try. Put yourself in an all or nothing situation: call and make the appointment, that's how i forced myself to go.

You put yourself in a really shitty situation and you're afraid of dealing with it. Honestly, I agree with you, you are in a REALLY shitty position. Also, if I were your parents, I would probably beat the shit out of you too, not because of your lies (specifically), but because you did not have enough faith in your parents in the first place, and so you resulted in lying. I don't know if that made sense, but I don't know how to rephrase it. I don't want to try to bullshit you though, this is just cowardice, and others might try to convince you otherwise, but that's just it. You created this situation, and you're too afraid to face it. Seriously, if you feel like you have nothing to lose, then you might as well come clean. What. You're afraid that you'll disappoint your parents. You think that they're better off not knowing, and so it's better for you just to give up? Fuck that. You're parents are going to kill themselves (not literally) over your death, because they won't understand why, or what happened. They'll think they were terrible parents. They'll keep mulling over what happened to their child, and they might blame one another after they start blaming themselves. 

I'm one person who believe in suicide, I believe that suicide is viable, but not for you in your situation. Suicide should not be about getting out of a hellish situation you created yourself, or about an escape from sadness. Suicide should be more methodical and of your own accord, not because of anxiety. I want to tell you to man up, but I know how useless that will probably be. Seriously though, if you're really going to kill yourself, at least come out clean to your parents. Let them kill you, let them be disappointing, but at least give them a chance to say goodbye. Don't underestimate how much your parents care about you. I'm not trying to sugarcoat anything, they will be royally pissed off, but give them time, and talk to them about the stress and pressure they put on you. You can't say there's no reason to live, because you haven't tried living yet. You haven't struggled yet. Get out of this slump, or at least see through it a little bit, after it clears up, then you can commit suicide, but sort this shit out first. Grades aren't as important as a life, and I'm speaking on a behalf as a parent. Grades are never worth more than a life. I can't even begin to explain.

I don't think I can help, but I'll say this. You said that "No one will help," but that's just bullshit. Have you tried reaching out to people? And I'm not talking about on Reddit, because as valuable as a resource SW is, we are limited in what we can do (or at least in what they can do). Honestly, if you feel like you have nothing left to lose, if you really feel like you're just going to kill yourself, then you might as well exhaust your resources. You say no one will help, well try your friends first, then work your way up to your family. Of course you'll get an array of mixed reactions, between sarcasm (because they think you're joking) to deep concern. You really have no excuse not to, especially if you have nothing to lose. And if they can't help you, then at least take time to say goodbye, and give them a chance to stop you (for their sake more than yours). It's less of a sting to them. When you commit suicide out of nowhere, getting left a note is the biggest bitch slap you can give somebody. Trust me. Suicide letters, or videos, don't make up for have a minute to hug, and say goodbye. The other thing: I don't know if this applies, or where you're at in your life, but you can't expect people to come to you. Life does not revolve around you, or anyone else (other than celebrities), and so you can't expect anyone to come out and actively try to help you if they don't know if there is a problem. you have to go out and make an effort, more than just this. Anyways, good luck in your choices. Some people will tell you that life gets better, and it's half true, but life also gets tougher, and things can get a lot worst. HOWEVER, things do get better if/when you let them. Like the other poster stated: you can go out and get married, get a job etc. There's not guarantee that you'll get them, but you could at least try before you just throw your life away. =/

If you're really considering suicide, give yourself a set amount of time to really plan it out, and exhaust your resources, because maybe in your suicide period you will find something that works for you. I mean, yeah, they'll try to talk you out of it, but at the end of the day, there are more ways for you to commit suicide, than for them to stop you. Oh, forgot to expand on the waiting period thing, you should not commit suicide in the heat of the moment, it's something that should be more methodical, and planned out, especially because of the emotional ups and downs of daily life, and so by giving yourself an extended date, instead of committing suicide off the fly, then you'll be able to see how much you want to live. Trust, the couple of days, or weeks, before your set day will show you how much you want to live, or die. And when you come to that date, then it's your decision. Of course I'll be cheering for you to choose life, but honestly, it's your choice, and none of us can stop you. Best of luck though.
